title: Product Co-Purchase Analysis
description: Find product pairs that were **bought together in the same order at least twice**. Show both product names and the number of orders containing both. This is a simplified market basket analysis.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE order_items (item_id INT, order_id INT, product_id INT); CREATE TABLE products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR(100)); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Laptop'),(2,'Mouse'),(3,'Keyboard'),(4,'Monitor'),(5,'Webcam'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,1,1),(2,1,2),(3,1,3),(4,2,1),(5,2,2),(6,3,1),(7,3,3),(8,3,4),(9,4,2),(10,4,3),(11,5,1),(12,5,2),(13,5,3),(14,6,3),(15,6,4),(16,7,2),(17,7,5);
solution_sql: SELECT p1.name AS product_a, p2.name AS product_b, COUNT(*) AS co_purchase_count FROM order_items oi1 JOIN order_items oi2 ON oi1.order_id = oi2.order_id AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id JOIN products p1 ON oi1.product_id = p1.product_id JOIN products p2 ON oi2.product_id = p2.product_id GROUP BY p1.name, p2.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY co_purchase_count DESC, p1.name

test_cases.description: Pairs with count>=2: Laptop+Mouse(3), Laptop+Keyboard(3), Mouse+Keyboard(3), Keyboard+Monitor(2) = 4 pairs

hints: Self-join order_items on the same order_id but with oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id to avoid duplicate pairs (A,B) and (B,A) and self-pairs.
Join the products table twice (once for each side of the pair) to get product names, then GROUP BY names and filter with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2.
explanation: The self-join oi1.order_id = oi2.order_id finds all product pairs in the same order; oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id ensures each pair appears exactly once. Laptop+Mouse appear together in orders 1, 2, 5 (count=3). Laptop+Keyboard: orders 1, 3, 5 (count=3). Mouse+Keyboard: orders 1, 4, 5 (count=3). Keyboard+Monitor: orders 3, 6 (count=2). Four pairs qualify.
